text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zagreb will continue to cooperate with the war crimes tribunal in the Hague although it is dissatisfied with the way the tribunal has treated Croatia and its suspects, the government said at its weekly session.

- Croatian army and police patrolling the southern border with Montenegro are carefully monitoring the deployment of Yugoslav Army units in Montenegro, where the Yugoslav navy has already clashed with local police.
- Presidents Franjo Tudjman of Croatia and Alija Izetbegovic of Bosnia may yet again postpone their meeting, scheduled for June 30, officials in Sarajevo say.

- The government mandates Finance Minister Bozo Prka to report within a week on whether Croatia will cancel its demand to the World Bank for a $30 million loan, which the Bank has recently postponed upon a U.S. request.

- Ivan Supek, head of the Croatian Academy of Arts and Sciences, replies to President Tudjman's recent open letter, carried in all state media, which accused Supek of defaming Tudjman and calling for his assassination. "I've been a peacemaker and humanist for 50 years, which excludes any violence," Supek says.
- This year's tourist season may require an additional workforce of 8,000 people, mostly to work in restaurants as cooks, assistants and waiters.
- Inspectors of Ministry of communications shut down transmitter of Marjan TV in Split, the oldest private TV station in Croatia, because it did not undergo necessary technical tests.
- After the Mediterranean Games in Bari, Croatia, with 33 medals, has become a Mediterranean (sports) superpower.
- Harassment of children in Split, especially by their own mothers, in on the rise. Number of cases up by 200 percent, according to the Split probation centre.

- Leaders of the ruling HDZ party met to discuss the reintegration of the predominantly Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia. The return of all state institutions and people to the area must be speeded up, the HDZ said.
- Croatian parliament debates proposed law on social welfare, with respect to the budget, and concludes higher employment is best way to fight poverty.
- A review slams performance of "Redemption" by American Ron Athey, staged at the annual Eurokaz theatre show in Zagreb, as nauseating pornography.
- The government amends agreement it signed with Bosnia in March by regulating the opening of four border crossings with Bosnia's Serb Republic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
